Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses, while security forces engaged them in an exchange of fireAccording to officials, large number of militants armed with sophisticated weapons attacked Chawangkining Naga village around 10.30pm, hours after two Kuki women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in neighbouring Tamenglong district.CRPF personnel deployed in the nearby area returned fire, triggering intermittent firing that continued for nearly six hours until around 4.30am on Wednesday."Intermittent firing was reported for nearly six hours till 4.30 am on Wednesday. The CRPF returned fire, preventing the militants from entering the village," the official said, adding that two wooden houses at the periphery of the village were, however, burnt down.The attack came hours after two Kuki-Zo women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district on Tuesday.The deceased were identified as 28-year-old nursing graduate Kimjalhai Singson and 76-year-old Phalneichong Sitlhou, both residents of the same village.Sitlhou, a widow, was shot while gathering firewood at her farm, while Singson, who had recently completed her nursing course, had returned home to help her parents with farming.Senior Naga leader and Naga Peoples' Front legislator Awangbou Newmai on Wednesday condemned the killing of the two women and the burning of houses at Chawangkining."These kinds of barbaric and senseless acts will never bring any good things to any community," Newmai said in a statement.A Kuki MLA from Saikul constituency in Kangpokpi district also condemned the killings and said one of the victims had recently graduated in nursing.Alleging the involvement of NSCN-IM and ZUF-K cadres in the killings, she said, "The killing of the innocent women is an act of sheer brutality that cannot be justified by any political cause, ideology or grievance."
Article Summary: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses. The attack came hours after two Kuki-Zo women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district.

Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:
Earlier, the Bombay HC ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Salian's death.

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian. No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.

Article Title: How fish has BJP's plate full in West Bengal
Article Text:
Bengal CM prayed at Kalighat temple and had fish-basanti pulao prasad.

From Liluah to Kalighat

Dhirendra Shastri on Durga Puja.

BJP pushback

BJP dismissed all anxieties over Durga Puja.

The not-so-new ‘maach-bhaat’ row

The Bengal and Bengali dilemma for Suvendu

The larger question for BJP

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari last week offered prayers at the Kalighat Temple on the occasion of 'Kaushiki Amavasya' and partook of a traditional bhog that included fish and 'basanti pulao'. Interestingly, the timing of the visit gave the ritual a political context.The meal came amid a political controversy over Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's recent appeal to Bengali Hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. As expected, the remarks kicked up a political storm, forcing the BJP’s Bengal unit to publicly distinguish itself from Dhirendra Shastri’s position on food.Chief minister Adhikari, who had shared a stage with Shastri earlier this month and invited him to establish a centre in Bengal, then got into the balancing act.“A religious figure is entitled to express his opinion, but whether people accept it or not is a personal matter,” the chief minister said after his Kalighat visit.Adhikari also referred to his own practices, saying he follows a sattvik diet on Ashtami and during Kartik, while accepting fish offered to Goddess Kali as bhog and goat meat as prasad."A saint or a religious leader is entitled to express their opinion. People may choose to accept it or not. On Mahashtami, when I worship Maa Durga, I consume sattvik food. During the month of Kartik also, I consume sattvik food. At the same time, as a Bengali, I accept the bhog offered to Maa with fish. I also accept the prasad of goat sacrifice. Today, whatever was offered to Maa in the afternoon, the temple priests gave me the same. There was fish head and fried fish, along with basanti pulao," he said.All this began on September 4, when Adhikari shared the stage with Shastri at a Hanumant Katha programme at the Liluah Workshop Ground in Howrah.Addressing Shastri, Adhikari said: "Baba Maharaj Ji, please open a centre here. There should also be a Bageshwar Dham centre. This is the land of saints and of spiritual awakening."Two days later, on September 6, Shastri appealed to Hindus in Bengal not to sell, cook or eat non-vegetarian food near Durga Puja idols during Navratri. He described those consuming such food as "pakhandi" and called for opposition to the practice."I am appealing to the Hindus of Bengal, that during Navratri, even if you don't keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell or consume non-veg near the idols. I do not like it when dirty non-vegetarian food is eaten during Durga Puja and at gatherings linked to the festivities. I want the Hindus of Kolkata to awaken and boycott such people. These people cannot be considered religious; they are pakhandi (hypocrites). Wake up and expel those people," he appealed.The remarks triggered criticism from the opposition and prompted the Bengal BJP to distance itself from the dietary prescription.State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya said no one could decide what Bengalis should eat."How can Bengalis not have fish and meat?" he said, adding that people in Bengal would continue with their traditional food practices. He also invoked Swami Vivekananda while defending the consumption of meat and fish in Bengal’s religious traditions.Other BJP leaders, including Dilip Ghosh, also said food choices were a matter of personal preference and referred to the place of meat in some Bengali religious traditions.The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also found itself navigating the controversy following statements made during an interactive session with Kolkata puja organizers. Swami Nirgunananda, a member of the VHP's central advisory council, had suggested that non-vegetarian food stalls be kept away from the immediate area around Durga idols and situated in designated spaces outside pandals to maintain sanctity and cleanliness.When his comments were interpreted as an official organisational diktat restricting meat sales, VHP International president Alok Kumar issued a formal clarification. "Vishva Hindu Parishad has not issued any directions regarding the arrangements at Durga Puja pandals... worship of the Goddess should take place according to tradition and the atmosphere should be one of love and devotion," it said.The Kalighat temple is associated with Bengal's 'Shakta' tradition, in which offerings can include fish and meat. The bhog included several varieties of fish, along with other vegetarian dishes and goat meat.That tradition sits somewhat differently from the vegetarian dietary practices associated with Navratri in several parts of north and west India.The controversy over Shastri's remarks comes months after fish and meat had already become part of the BJP-TMC contest over Bengali identity during the assembly election campaign.Mamata Banerjee repeatedly alleged during the campaign that a BJP government would restrict what Bengalis could eat. At a rally in Purulia on March 29, she said: "BJP says can't eat fish, meat, eggs." She subsequently argued that restrictions on meat and fish sales in some BJP-ruled states showed what could lie ahead for Bengal.The issue became prominent enough for senior BJP leaders to address it directly. Amit Shah clarified that "consumption of fish, eggs will not be stopped" if the BJP came to power in Bengal, calling Mamata's claim a rumour.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also sought to engage with the issue, though from a different direction. At a rally in Haldia, he spoke about Bengal's fish production and said the state could become self-sufficient in fish under a BJP government. "In 15 years, TMC couldn't even give you fish. We created a separate ministry for fisheries," he said, contrasting Bengal's production with that of Bihar and Assam.The BJP’s campaign also included more visible efforts to counter the perception that it was opposed to Bengali food habits. Leaders publicly ate fish and meat, while BJP candidates and workers used fish in campaign imagery. On Poila Boishakh, TMC organised a "Maach-Bhaat-e-Bangali" procession, alleging that the BJP would impose restrictions on fish and meat.The argument did not remain confined to the two parties. TMC leaders presented food as part of the broader question of Bengali identity. BJP leaders, in turn, sought to emphasise that dietary choices would remain a matter of personal freedom.Months after the BJP swept Bengal in assembly elections, the opposition has sought to use the same "outsider" charge to try and alienate the saffron party from the voters. Congress filed a police complaint against Shastri, alleging that his comments hurt Bengali sentiments, while invoking the “outsider” argument that the TMC had used against the BJP during the election. Congress’s complaint described his remarks as an affront to Bengali traditions and social harmony.The TMC, which had made fish and meat part of its cultural-identity campaign against the BJP, is also again using the remark against the party.As CM, however, Adhikari has also taken a position on protests against Shastri.On September 10, he directed the Kolkata Police commissioner to arrest those who allegedly burnt Shastri’s photographs during a protest in Bhawanipur. "Not in Bengal," he said, making clear that burning photographs as a form of protest would not be tolerated.The move has produced another political contest. Congress has criticised the arrests and accused the government of protecting Shastri while acting against those protesting his remarks. One Congress leader, Atanu Das, was subsequently arrested.The recent row has brought an old question back for the BJP in Bengal: how does the party's Hindu politics sit with the state's own traditions?Bengal has a strong Shakta tradition, centred on Kali and Durga. In this tradition, the line between what is considered religious and what is considered non-vegetarian is not always drawn in the same way as it is in northern/western India. Fish, and in some places meat, can be part of offerings and rituals.That makes food an unusually sensitive issue in Bengal. And for many Bengalis, it is tied to family customs, festivals and a sense of what is distinctly 'Bengali'.Suvendu Adhikari is leading the first BJP government in Bengal. For now, he might be able to shut down critics by consuming fish bhog at Kalighat. But it will be interesting to see how he manages BJP's national Hindu politics in Bengal while also balancing the "Bengaliness".
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari last week offered prayers at the Kalighat Temple and partook of a traditional bhog that included fish and 'basanti pulao' The meal came amid a political controversy over Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's recent appeal to Bengali Hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja.

Article Title: 'See how many allies of Pakistan were in that room': Omar Abdullah praises Centre over Pahalgam condemnation at Brics
Article Text:
Omar praises Centre for Brics

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre and recently held Brics Summit in Delhi. Omar Abdullah said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win.J&K CM remarks came after India hosted the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, bringing together several world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The National Conference leader particularly highlighted the inclusion of the Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics New Delhi Declaration, pointing out that the statement came in the presence of countries that share close ties with Pakistan."That is something for the Government of India, and particularly for the foreign ministry, to talk about. The fact that Pahalgam itself was condemned is a big thing. Please see how many allies of Pakistan were in that room. Therefore, for even Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy," Omar Abdullah said.J&K CM Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India’s fronts with Pakistan and China.Reacting to the ministry of defence’s report on the operational situation along the Northern Front, he said any move to reduce troop deployments along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) or Line of Control (LoC) would be a positive development, particularly for people living in border areas."Anything that reduces tension along the Line of Control or the Line of Actual Control is a good step, particularly for those people who live close to it. We know that living near the LoC or LAC is extremely difficult for people. If there is any step that reduces deployments along the Line of Actual Control, that is a good step. Similarly, we hope that, over time, things will also get better along the Line of Control," he added.The comments came days after the Brics Summit concluded in the national capital. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the New Delhi Declaration had been unanimously adopted and called the gathering as a huge summit.Days ago, senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor backed the Brics Summit as an important diplomatic opportunity for India, appearing to differ with party colleague P Chidambaram, who questioned whether recent Brics meetings have produced tangible benefits.Tharoor highlighted the diplomatic value of India hosting leaders from across the Brics grouping and its partner countries, stressing the importance of such engagements for New Delhi.Chidambaram, however, had questioned the outcomes of recent Brics summits.“I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results.”“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram’s remarks triggered a political response from the BJP, which accused the Congress of questioning an event that, it said, reflected India’s growing standing on the global stage.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre. He said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win. Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India's fronts with Pakistan and China.

Article Title: ‘Umar Khalid is a nationalist’: B K Hariprasad’s remark sparks BJP attack
Article Text:
Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a nationalist.





BENGALURU: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad Tuesday called jailed activist Umar Khalid a “nationalist” and criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University (NLSIU).“ABVP has no right to speak about Khalid because ABVP adores Nathuram Godse, who is anti-national and the first terrorist of the country,” Hariprasad said.The remarks came after ABVP in Bengaluru demanded cancellation of the proposed screening of filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s documentary, ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’, at NLSIU. The documentary was scheduled to be screened Monday by the law and society committee, a student organisation at the university. NLSIU later said it had to reschedule the event due to “logistical and security considerations”.The screening was to express solidarity with Khalid and to mark six years since his imprisonment without trial under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots.BJP hit back at Hariprasad’s remarks, calling them deeply condemnable. In New Delhi, Sambit Patra, MP, linked Hariprasad’s remarks to Congress’ past interactions with Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik.“Just think about it: this is the same Umar Khalid,” Patra said. “During the Citizenship Amendment Act protests in Feb 2020, so many people were killed in Delhi. A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.
Article Summary: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a ‘nationalist’ He criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University.

Article Title: Swept away by Ganga 15 days ago, Bihar woman found in UP
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For 15 days, Sunaina Devi (55) survived on river water and the fragile shelter of a half-submerged thatched hut, after being swept 50km downstream by the monsoon-swollen Ganga. She was found alive Monday by fishermen who heard her cries.Devi, from Kapurpatti village in Bihar's Buxar district, had gone to bathe on Aug 30 when the current pulled her under. Her son, Govinda Gond, filed a missing person report at Itarhi police station. Her family did not know she had drifted across the state border into Chain Chhapra village in UP's Ballia, on the other side of the river, soon after falling in.In Chain Chhapra, Devi managed to grab an abandoned hut in a field and pull herself up. Surrounded by floodwater, she survived by drinking from the same Ganga that had nearly drowned her.On Monday she collapsed and slipped once again into floodwater. Mallah fishermen in boats heard her chants of "Shivguru-Sh-ivguru", spotted her behind sarpat grass and pulled her aboard.Hunger strike studies in British Medical Journal say with water intake, the body can survive without food for 21 to 40 days."It was miraculous," Haldi SHO Rajiv Kumar Rai told TOI. Police gave her food and water and determined her identity.The family had feared the worst. "There was no update for so many days we genuinely thought we'd lost her," Govinda said.Police said relatives broke down in tears when they saw her. "They were not expecting to find her alive. The reunion was emotional and raw," Rai said.Her husband, Janardhan, a farmer, told TOI, "Deep down, there was still a flickering hope."Devi is still dazed. "It feels like my mind stops at one place. It was very difficult to be alone for so many days. I didn't know I had such strength in me," she says.Her family says she remains weak. Doctors expect the disorientation to ease in a few days.
Article Summary: Sunaina Devi (55) survived on river water and the fragile shelter of a half- submerged thatched hut. She was found alive Monday by fishermen who heard her cries. Devi, from Kapurpatti village in Bihar's Buxar district, had gone to bathe on Aug 30.

Article Title: Indo-US joint military exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 begins in Uttarakhand, Rajasthan simultaneously
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The opening ceremony of 22nd edition of India-US joint military exercise ‘Yudh Abhyas 2026’ was held on Tuesday at Auli foreign training node in Uttarakhand.Major General Amaresh Gunjan, General Officer Commanding, 14 Infantry Division and Colonel Benjamin Jackman, Commander, 1st Infantry Brigade Combat Team, 11th Airborne Division, US Army, addressed the participating contingents of 600 personnel from both countries. The exercise is simultaneously being conducted at Auli and Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan.The exercise is aimed at enhancing the joint military capability of both armies for employment of Integrated Battle Groups in mountainous and semi-mountainous terrain, with emphasis on infantry-dominated operations. It will strengthen interoperability, facilitate exchanges of best operational practices and strengthen joint planning and execution, a defence ministry’s release said on Tuesday.Technology infusion will form a key focus area. The training will include the employment of drones and autonomous systems for surveillance and reconnaissance as well as demonstration of contemporary weapon systems will be undertaken at Mahajan field firing ranges, it said.Subject matter experts from both Armies will also exchange views on emerging technologies and developments in multi-domain warfare. The exercise provides an opportunity for both Armies to share tactics, techniques and procedures; and enhance their ability to undertake coordinated military operations across varied terrain and operational environment.
Article Summary: The opening ceremony of 22nd edition of India-US joint military exercise ‘Yudh Abhyas 2026’ was held on Tuesday at Auli foreign training node in Uttarakhand. The exercise is aimed at enhancing the joint military capability of both armies for employment of Integrated Battle Groups.

Article Title: Omar praises India’s foreign policy over Brics mention of Pahalgam, slams Centre on UCC
Article Text:
Omar praises Centre for Brics

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: The condemnation of Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics declaration earned praise for India’s foreign policy from Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday, but the National Conference vice-president hit out at the Centre over what he called an attempt to bring in the Uniform Civil Code through the back door.“The fact that Pahalgam was condemned (at the Brics summit) is significant. Consider how many allies of Pakistan were present in that room. Therefore, for Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy,” Omar said while talking to reporters in Srinagar.About China praising India’s foreign policy, he said India should not “seek certificates of approval from other countries”. “The danger with this approach is that tomorrow, if China says something critical about our foreign policy, what will we do then? ... We cannot cherry-pick,” he said.On reports that China had scaled back troops along the Line of Actual Control, he said “...anything that reduces tension along the LoC or the LAC is a positive step”.The J&K CM, however, was critical of the central govt for trying to implement the UCC in all NDA-governed states. “Something of this nature should not be decided by individual states; it has to be decided by the country as a whole,” he said, adding that the Centre should introduce a bill in Parliament instead of trying to bring in UCC through the back door.Accusing the Modi govt of bypassing Parliament, Omar said, “If they have the numbers, they should bring the UCC bill to Parliament. Why are they doing it through individual states?”The remarks came in the backdrop of Union home minister Amit Shah’s statement on Sunday that the UCC will be implemented in all 21 BJP-NDA states before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Omar pointed out that NDA partners like TDP, JD(U) and LJP (RV) had chosen to be circumspect about the idea. “Given that even some of their own allies do not support it, I do not think they will be able to get it (UCC bill) passed in Parliament. This is probably the reason why they are choosing this route,” he added.
Article Summary: The condemnation of Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics declaration earned praise for India’s foreign policy from Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah. Omar hit out at the Centre over what he called an attempt to bring in the Uniform Civil Code through the back door.

Article Title: DMK submits privilege petition against law minister over remarks on Stalin, Karunanidhi
Article Text:
DMK submits petition to Speaker

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: DMK leader Ethirajulu Vajjaravelu on Tuesday said the party had submitted a petition to the Speaker seeking breach of privilege action against Law Minister Nirmal Kumar over statements he made in the Legislative Assembly about leaders who were not present in the House.“We had submitted a petition to the Speaker seeking breach of privilege action against Law Minister Nirmal Kumar, as he made statements in the Legislative Assembly containing false information about leaders who were not present in the House,” Vajjaravelu said.He said discussing people who were absent from the House or making allegations against them was against the rules and conventions of the Legislative Assembly.“Discussing persons who are not present in the House or making allegations against them is against the rules and conventions of the Legislative Assembly...We have urged the Speaker to take appropriate action in the matter...,” he added.Earlier last week, the DMK staged protests across the state, condemning Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay over his alleged “scurrilous remarks” targeting late party patriarch M Karunanidhi and party president M K Stalin The party had earlier described Vijay’s Assembly speech as strongly condemnable, alleging that it trivialised Karunanidhi, late Union minister Murasoli Maran, the DMK and Stalin’s sacrifices.Vijay had targeted the DMK in the Assembly on September 7, alleging serious and organised corruption during its previous regimes.He cited the Sarkaria Commission report in his criticism of the DMK government led by late chief minister M Karunanidhi several decades ago, and also referred to late Union minister Murasoli Maran in this context.Vijay also cited official documents from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) shared with the state government over alleged corruption during the DMK’s 2021-26 tenure, naming then chief minister M K Stalin and his deputy Udhayanidhi Stalin.Meanwhile, Law Minister Nirmal Kumar disputed the DMK’s long-standing claim that Stalin was detained under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) during the Emergency.Kumar said there was no official record indicating that Stalin’s detention was under MISA and claimed he was arrested over remarks concerning late prime minister Indira Gandhi and her 20-point programme, announced after the Emergency was declared by the then Congress-led government at the Centre.On Saturday, Kumar challenged Stalin to produce his official detention order, reiterating his claim that the former chief minister had not been imprisoned under MISA during the Emergency.
Article Summary: DMK leader Ethirajulu Vajjaravelu said the party had submitted a petition to the Speaker seeking breach of privilege action against Law Minister Nirmal Kumar. He said discussing people who were absent from the House or making allegations against them was against the rules and conventions of the Legislative Assembly.

Article Title: ‘No reason to make haste’: JD(U) takes cautious stand on UCC, says it will decide after studying Bill
Article Text:
File photo: Bihar deputy chief minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary

JD(U) distances itself from RJD’s opposition

Sanjay Jha to hold talks with Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: Janata Dal (United) on Tuesday adopted a cautious position on the proposed Uniform Civil Code (UCC), with Bihar deputy chief minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary saying the party will first study the legislation and will not oppose it “for no reason” if its provisions are found to be unexceptionable.Chaudhary, who is also a former state Assembly speaker, said the JD(U) would take a decision after consulting its coalition partners in the BJP-led NDA in Bihar. NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Tuesday granted Swatantra Bhardwaj interim bail for three weeks in connection with the alleged assault of the father of a Dalit student-activist during a protest at Jantar Mantar.Bhardwaj is facing charges in connection with the alleged assault during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar in June. He was arrested in Uttar Pradesh on September 5 and has been in judicial custody.The court's interim bail order comes a day after Bhardwaj's counsel argued that his arrest was politically motivated and claimed that the complainant had attacked Bhardwaj during the incident.During Monday's hearing, advocate Umesh Sharma told the court that a video purportedly showed the complainant attacking Bhardwaj."Police ko wo video nazar nahi aa raha... The action followed protests by CJP leaders, the student and her father outside the Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest.Bhardwaj had also claimed in an interview that he had “cracked the skull” of the girl's father during the protest and escaped arrest because of his political connections. He had claimed proximity to NDA leaders Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan, though Paswan denied the claim and filed a separate complaint against him for allegedly misusing his name.

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh Monday hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly, saying the unison adaptation was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi Calling "inclusive and human-centric approach" an hallmark of the summit, the defence minister laid emphasis on how the bloc put Global South "at the centre, not at the margins, championing a more inclusive, representative and balanced world order"."Rooted in our civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiv Kutumbkam, India has once again shown that leadership is not about having the loudest voice, but the strongest consensus," the Union minister said, adding: "As India leads, the world listens."In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The talks were complicated by differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia conflict. An earlier meeting of Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had also ended without a joint statement.The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi after a rare meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the summit.The meeting took place as the conflict continued and helped ease the differences threatening consensus.The declaration used carefully balanced language to address the concerns of both countries. It expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities operating under full International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, describing such actions as violations of international law and relevant IAEA resolutions. The wording amounted to an implicit criticism of US and Israeli strikes on Iran and was important in securing Tehran’s approval.The leaders also recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to maintain the smooth movement of global trade, supply chains and energy in line with international law.Official sources said India conducted prolonged negotiations at several levels to bridge the differences between Iran and the UAE. Other member-states also supported the effort, keen to ensure that the summit ended with a joint declaration rather than another failure to reach consensus.The agreement recalled the last-minute G20 declaration adopted in New Delhi in 2023 during the Russia-Ukraine war. That statement used carefully worded language urging countries not to use force to seize territory without directly naming Russia.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly. Singh said it was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration.

Article Title: FDA suspends Mumbai's iconic Cafe Mondegar licence over hygiene lapses
Article Text:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has temporarily revoked the license of Cafe Mondegar





MUMBAI: FDA on Tuesday suspended the licence of Café Mondegar, the iconic 94-year-old restaurant in Colaba, for hygiene and structural violations.Some of the issues flagged included temperature control failures—hot foods kept below 60°C, cold storage above 5°C, improper thawing, and slow cooling—damp floors; defective drainage near food preparation areas, posing cross-contamination risks; and inadequate equipment sanitisation.The restaurant declined to comment, saying its manager had left for the day.FDA also suspended the licences of nine other establishments— Ruhafza Bakery (Khar West), Chandru’s Pure Ghee Sweets (Andheri West), Sharma Dairy & Fast Food (Andheri West), Punjabi Chandu Halwai LLP (Grant Road East), Shri Narayan Dairy (Vile Parle West), Gulshan Dairy Farm (Khar West), Tribhuvan Dairy Farm (Ghatkopar West), Mahavir Cashew & Foods Pvt Ltd (Ghatkopar East), and Agrawal Sweet Mart (Jogeshwari East).Officials said keeping in mind possible large-scale adulteration or hygiene violations during the festive season, a joint FDA-BMC workshop was held for 110 self-help groups engaged in making modaks. They said assistant commissioners and food safety officers guided attendees on good hygiene and manufacturing practices, as well as methods to prevent cross-contamination.Such workshops were also arranged for office-bearers and volunteers of various Ganesh mandals across the city. “This was to ensure that prasad distributed to devotees is prepared and served in a safe, hygienic and healthy manner, taking necessary food safety precautions. A total of five workshops were held at various locations, with participation from 320 Ganesh mandals and member organisations,” FDA said.
Article Summary: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has temporarily revoked the license of Cafe Mondegar. Issues flagged included temperature control failures, improper thawing, and slow cooling.
