Article Title: Jarange’s Mumbai stir: Health concerns grow after 18-day fast; Fadnavis flags protest timing
Article Text:
Jarange accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community and vowed to continue the agitation.

— with inputs from Chaitanya Marpakwar & Abhishek Choudhari





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Tuesday began his march from Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district to Mumbai, setting the stage for another showdown with state govt. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed for a protest that does not disrupt Ganeshotsav.Eighteen days into his indefinite hunger strike, Jarange left his Jalna village around noon and announced that he would resume his fast at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Sept 19. His convoy is expected to travel more than 400 km through Beed, Ahilyanagar, Pune and Raigad before reaching the state capital.The march comes amid uncertainty over permission for the proposed protest. Mumbai Police have already rejected two applications seeking permission for an indefinite hunger strike at Azad Maidan. A fresh application, this time seeking permission for a gathering of 50 people and assuring compliance with all conditions, remains under consideration.Addressing reporters on Tuesday, Fadnavis said, “Police had rejected Jarange’s application seeking permission to protest in Mumbai. Police will decide on any fresh application based on its merits.”The chief minister maintained that govt had already addressed most of the movement’s demands.“Govt has accepted 12 of the 13 demands raised by the Maratha protesters that were legally valid,” Fadnavis said, adding that legal constraints prevented action on the remaining demands.“I feel that instead of taking such a position during the festive days, they should take a decision so that people do not face any inconvenience,” he added.Jarange, however, accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community and vowed to continue the agitation.“I will not surrender before govt,” he said, adding the protest was aimed at securing justice for Maratha youth and future generations.Earlier in the day, Jarange underwent a health check-up, offered prayers at a Hanuman temple and then set out with a small convoy of supporters. Crowds gathered along the route, raising slogans and greeting the activist. The response slowed his movement considerably, with the convoy covering barely 22 km in nearly six hours before heading towards Patoda in Beed district.Concern over Jarange’s health continues to grow. He has reportedly stopped accepting medical treatment and saline after police denied permission for the Mumbai protest. His supporters fear his condition may worsen during the journey.His wife, Sumitra Jarange, blamed govt for forcing him back onto the streets. “Govt is incapable of understanding us. If they had taken decisions earlier, he would not have set out for Mumbai. When every person has the right to agitate, how can the govt deny permission for our agitation?” she asked.The state has deployed a Special Protection Unit officer and a constable to accompany Jarange throughout the march.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde , speaking publicly on the issue for the first time since the Mumbai agitation was announced, said, “Govt is taking care that Ganesh devotees do not face any inconvenience. Earlier, 58 morchas were held, and the world took note of those morchas. No one was ever inconvenienced or allowed to face any inconvenience through those morchas. Therefore, we want everyone to ensure that no one is inconvenienced during Ganeshotsav,” Shinde said.The Jarange agitation was also discussed at Tuesday’s cabinet meeting. Minister Shambhuraj Desai defended the administration’s handling of the issue, saying it had honoured commitments made during talks with the activist and had undertaken extensive work to trace Kunbi records through the Justice Shinde Committee.OBC groups and MoS Ashish Jaiswal too backed govt’s stand on Jarange’s agitation on Tuesday, arguing that most of his demands have already been met and accused him of prolonging a now “non-issue” movement. However, NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar blamed govt for failing to engage meaningfully with the Maratha quota activist.MoS Ashish Jaiswal said govt had established the required scrutiny mechanism for Maratha reservation claims and that grievances should be addressed through legal channels rather than street protests. He alleged that Jarange’s continued agitation was being driven by “malice and prejudice” and was creating unnecessary confusion.OBC Mahasangh president Babanrao Taywade said most of Jarange’s demands had been fulfilled except those pending before courts. He argued that the agitation was unlikely to receive public support and accused Jarange of holding people hostage to a protest.Rohit Pawar, however, said govt was responsible for the impasse. He argued that the lack of sustained dialogue had pushed Jarange back onto the streets and questioned the police decision to deny permission for a protest in Mumbai. “Holding a protest is a constitutional right,” Pawar said.
Article Summary: Eighteen days into his indefinite hunger strike, Manoj Jarange left his Jalna village around noon. He announced that he would resume his fast at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Sept 19. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed for a protest that does not disrupt Ganeshotsav. Jarange accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community.

Article Title: Disha case FIR: Aaditya Thackeray, other netas, cops need probe; RG Kar case CBI officer assigned to investigate
Article Text:
The CBI has registered an FIR in the 2020 Disha Salian death case

RG Kar case officer to head CBI investigation





MUMBAI: With CBI filing an FIR in the 2020 Disha Salian death case, its investigators are expected to first scrutinise documents and allegations, record statements including of police personnel who handled the initial inquiry, examine the scene and key witnesses, and carry out technical analysis before identifying suspects for questioning.Disha, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput ’s manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai. A week later, Sushant was found dead at his Bandra flat. Citing “suspicious circumstances,” her father petitioned the high court seeking a murder probe. Satish Salian recorded his statement before CBI last week, and it was converted into the FIR on Sept 13.A CBI official said the FIR was registered pursuant to the court’s direction and no accused have been named at this stage, adding that names would be included if involvement is established during the probe.The FIR alleges that some public servants and police officers need to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders. It also calls for the questioning of the autopsy and forensic officials besides several others, including the building’s security guards.The FIR claims: “The persons whose roles require investigation in connection with the commission of the principal offences, criminal conspiracy, subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story, and suppression, destruction and/or fabrication of evidence include Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, Dino Morea, Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya Thackeray’s bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, Sachin Vaze, Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur, Uddhav Thackeray, Anil Deshmukh, API Ashok Devadhe, PI Jagdev Kalapad, PI Shailendra Nagarkar, PI Chimaji Adhav, PI Arjun Rajane, concerned officers of Malvani Police Station”.Satish Salian’s advocate Nilesh Ojha had alleged that Disha had information about Aaditya Thackeray’s illegal activities, shared it with Sushant Singh Rajput, who discussed it with Rhea Chakraborty, and that it was then passed to Aaditya Thackeray, after which the alleged offence and cover-up took place.With Salian alleging lapses, the high court pulled up Mumbai police for not filing an FIR in the last six years and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the probe. It observed that the police probe “raised more questions than answers.”The high court had also taken note of the fact that the post-mortem report or the accidental death report had not been given to Disha’s family. On Sept 2, ordering a CBI probe, the court directed the agency that no one should be named as accused unless there was evidence against them.
Article Summary: The CBI has registered an FIR in the 2020 Disha Salian death case. Disha, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput ’s manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building. Citing “suspicious circumstances,” her father petitioned the high court seeking a murder probe.

Article Title: 70-year-old man detained as illegal Bangladeshi gets bail after 3 months in jail
Article Text:
An elderly man detained for three months was granted bail by a court (Representative image)





KOLKATA: A 70-year-old man who spent nearly three months in a holding centre and jail after being detained on June 20 on suspicion of being an illegal Bangladeshi national was granted bail by an Islampur court on Monday.Jalil Akhtar, who produced nine documents, including his name in Bengal 2026 SIR electoral roll and EPIC card, to establish his Indian citizenship, faces a deportation order issued by the local Foreigners Registration Officer (FRO). Police took him to the border three times, but the BSF could not deport him as he maintained he was an Indian citizen.Islampur Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Jamshed Shaikh, in a six-page order, wrote: “From the materials in the CD (case diary), it appears that the deportation proceedings could not be completed as the accused...claimed himself to be an Indian citizen.” The magistrate also noted that a police verification report showed Akhtar’s EPIC details were available on the ECI-ERONET portal and in the final SIR 2026 electoral roll. His ration card and Aadhaar authentication were also found valid.The State opposed the bail, arguing that releasing Akhtar “may pose a potential threat to the security and interests of the State and may also give rise to an issue concerning national security.”The magistrate considered Akhtar’s age, lack of criminal antecedents, verified govt records and appearance in consecutive electoral rolls before granting bail on a Rs 10,000 bond. He was barred from leaving the court’s jurisdiction without prior intimation and directed not to tamper with evidence.His advocates, Firoz Ahamad and Syed Nafirul Islam, submitted evidence showing that Akhtar’s name has appeared in electoral rolls since 1995, including the 2002 and 2026 SIR lists.
Article Summary: Jalil Akhtar produced nine documents, including his name in Bengal 2026 SIR electoral roll and EPIC card, to establish his Indian citizenship. Police took him to the border three times, but the BSF could not deport him as he maintained he was an Indian citizen.

Article Title: Kanpur murder: 300 calls to contract killer put pharma trader’s son under scanner
Article Text:
Subrat and Shalu

Kanpur:





The role of murdered pharmaceutical businessman Vineet Minocha’s 34-year-old son Subrat has come under the scanner after police found that he allegedly refused to identify former servant and contract killer Vishal Gautam despite having spoken to him nearly 300 times in the three months before the crime. Investigators suspect Subrat deliberately withheld the identification to distance himself and his wife, Shalu (30), from the alleged conspiracy.Police found that Subrat and Gautam had spoken 309 times over the previous three months and exchanged 25 WhatsApp calls shortly before the murder. Subrat, Shalu and Vishal had also visited several places and shopped together around 20 days before Vineet (63) was stabbed 26 times on Sept 5, police said.Police said Subrat allegedly tried to delete call history and some numbers from his phone after the incident, further deepening suspicion.Investigators are probing why the couple had hired Vishal again for personal work without Vineet’s knowledge, despite the businessman having removed him earlier. Police also found that Shalu allegedly accompanied Vishal on the day of the murder to get a duplicate key made.Investigators suspect Shalu had hired Vishal for Rs 6 lakh and allegedly handed him the original key for the purpose.Police said Shalu had also informed Vishal when she, Subrat and their son would be away.On the day of the murder, police said Shalu and Vishal spoke 14 times. Police also recovered WhatsApp call records between Shalu and Vishal despite he allegedly deleting their chats.The investigation is also examining a viral video of Shalu dancing at a Kanpur lounge on the night Vineet was stabbed to death. Police are hunting for the person who recorded and circulated the clip to establish how and when it was filmed.DCP West S M Qasim Abidi said the clip came to light during the investigation into Vineet’s murder that took place in the Kalyanpur police station area on Sept 5.Shalu had been allegedly planning the murder for around three months and had gradually developed a rapport with Gautam. Gautam allegedly brought in Raj Kishore, 30, and the two entered the flat after posing as medicine delivery men. Police said they hid in a bedroom and planned to suffocate Vineet to make his death appear natural.When Vineet returned around 10.55pm and discovered them, the duo allegedly attacked him. Gautam and Kishore were arrested after an encounter on Sept 6, while Shalu was arrested the following night and sent to judicial custody.
Article Summary: Vineet Minocha’s 34-year-old son Subrat allegedly refused to identify former servant and contract killer Vishal Gautam. Investigators suspect Subrat deliberately withheld the identification to distance himself and his wife, Shalu (30), from the alleged conspiracy. Police found that Subrat and Vishal had spoken 309 times over the previous three months and exchanged 25 WhatsApp calls.

Article Title: Killed Kanpur pharma trader at bahu’s behest, ex-employee tells cops in jail
Article Text:
However, Shalu (30) denied involvement and remained silent on several questions, police said.





KANPUR: In the murder of 63-year-old pharmaceutical trader Vineet Minocha, police on Monday recorded the statements of his jailed daughter-in-law Shalu and former servant Vishal Gautam, with the latter reiterating that he carried out the killing at her behest.However, Shalu (30) denied involvement and remained silent on several questions, police said.Investigators are also examining her husband Subrat’s links with Vishal, with more than 300 conversations recorded between the two among the numbers analysed.Investigating officer and Kalyanpur police station in charge Keshav Tiwari questioned the two in jail after obtaining court permission. Police plan to seek custody remand for Shalu and Vishal and question them face-to-face with Subrat.Investigators are examining Vineet’s 2022 will, which made his wife, son and daughter stakeholders in his property but did not include daughter-in-law Shalu. Police are probing whether this could have prompted the alleged conspiracy.Police commissioner Raghubir Lal said investigators had obtained about 1,000 pages of call detail records for seven mobile numbers — two belonging to Vishal, three to Subrat and two to Shalu — covering the period from May 1 until the night of the murder.The records showed more than 300 conversations between Subrat and Vishal, the highest among the numbers examined, deepening police suspicion of Subrat. Investigators are analysing whom the suspects contacted before and after the murder, the duration of the calls and their relationships with those contacted.Vishal had earlier claimed that Shalu told him to name Subrat if he was caught, police said.According to Lal, Vishal bought a new SIM on Sept 3, two days before the murder, and discontinued his previous number that day. He subsequently called Shalu and Subrat.Police said Vishal and his aide Rajkishore escaped by scaling a wall at Ratan Orbit Apartment in Indira Nagar after the murder and then booked a taxi.They also called a friend five times. Investigators are gathering information about the friend to determine whether Vishal disclosed the murder or sought assistance.
Article Summary: Vishal Gautam reiterates that he carried out the killing at her behest. Shalu (30) denied involvement and remained silent on several questions, police said. More than 300 conversations recorded between her husband Subrat and Vishal.

Article Title: Inspired by web series ‘Pritam and Pedro’, Gurgaon man dupes MBA student of 25L
Article Text:
(Representative image) Gurgaon man was arrested for duping a management student of over twenty-four lakh rupees





MUMBAI: A 24-year-old man from Gurugram , who took inspiration from a web series on cybercrime, was arrested by the Bangur Nagar police for allegedly duping a management student of Rs 24.6 lakh. Alok K, the accused, had posed as a student counsellor and warned the victim that he would be debarred and his career prospects would be ruined if he did not pay up.Upon arrest, Alok told the police that he was inspired by the antagonist on the OTT show ‘Pritam and Pedro’ and had planned to use social engineering and impersonation to deceive the victim. He also intended to erase his digital footprint.The 21-year-old victim had enrolled in a distance-learning programme for an MBA (finance) with a prestigious management institute in Jan 2026. He paid an annual fee of Rs 1.12 lakh for admission and was assigned a seat by the institute.Soon after, the accused (Alok) got in touch with him over phone and introduced himself as a student counsellor. The two met at a cafe in Juhu after which Alok helped the student complete his admission formalities. The student started to trust him.In June, while the student was appearing for an exam online, an alert popped up on his device screen that copying had been detected.The student immediately called up Alok and informed him that he had not copied. On the last day of the exam, the same alert popped up again and the application crashed. At this, Alok called up the student and inquired whether he had been copying again. At this, the student once again denied any wrongdoing.The student grew nervous when Alok warned him that he would be debarred and blacklisted and would never be able to get an admission in any other university in future. Alok offered to sort out the matter and started demanding money. He also promised to refund fhe money if he was unable to do the job.The student transferred him Rs 24.6 lakh in installments. But Alok refunded him only Rs 1.15 lakh. When the student passed the exam but Alok continued to demand money, the student realized he had been taken for a ride. He then confided in his parents and they lodged a complaint at the Bangur Nagar police station earlier this month.Police surveilled Alok’s phone records and the money trail before tracking his location to Gurugram. He was arrested on Sept 11. Police said Alok used to previously work at a call centre that had been contracted by the management institute to coordinate with all students regarding admissions and counselling. He got the victim’s phone number from the call centre’s database and targeted him. Police have seized two cellphones from him.
Article Summary: Gurgaon man was arrested for duping a management student of over twenty-four lakh rupees. Alok K, the accused, posed as a student counsellor and warned the victim that he would be debarred and his career prospects would be ruined if he did not pay up.

Article Title: ‘Homes submerged’: Ken-Betwa protesters back on symbolic pyres over displacement
Article Text:
Displaced families continue their symbolic protest for proper compensation and rehabilitation.





BHOPAL: Displaced families affected by the Ken-Betwa, Majhgayan and Runjh projects continued their symbolic ‘Chita Andolan’ for the third day on Tuesday, demanding proper compensation and rehabilitation.The protest had earlier been suspended in July after the administration ended the agitation at Kupi village, but has now resumed amid rising water levels and concerns over houses and land being submerged.Sources said protesters are now also alleging irregularities in compensation distribution, including discrepancies in the assessment of land, houses and other assets, and are demanding an independent inquiry.They have also alleged that basic facilities were being disrupted to pressure them to withdraw the protest.The agitation is being led by families affected by multiple projects, with the Congress and Samajwadi Party extending support. Protesters have demanded that the administration hold talks with affected families and resolve compensation and rehabilitation claims before proceeding with further displacement.
Article Summary: Displaced families affected by the Ken-Betwa, Majhgayan and Runjh projects continued their symbolic ‘Chita Andolan’ for the third day on Tuesday. The protest had earlier been suspended in July after the administration ended the agitation at Kupi village.

Article Title: ‘Intended to kill her’: Chilling details emerge as cops say Gurgaon car collision with biker was deliberate
Article Text:
Kalyan Bainsla was arrested in Rajasthan for ramming his car into a biker





GURGAON: Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into a biker and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday morning, was arrested at Dausa in Rajasthan on Tuesday.A video from her bike's camera that Shivani Chauhan (27) uploaded online showed her being knocked down near Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station after the car repeatedly tried to get alongside her bike. Her Aprilia RS 457 slid across the road, while traffic sped past her.Bainsla's cousin Lovneesh (32), who was in the Maruti Ciaz with him on Sunday, was arrested too. After examining the video of the crash that Shivani shared, police have added the attempt to murder charge in the FIR against Bainsla. "He caused the collision deliberately from the side. He had an intention to kill her," DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar saidKumar clarified that the additional charge was based on evidence, not media pressure. "It's fortunate that she did not suffer any fatal injury. Only because she was wearing safety gear," he said.Police said Bainsla disappeared after giving a media interview when Shivani uploaded the video and it attracted widespread outrage. He crossed the border to Rajasthan with his cousin. Police sources said they even visited Pushkar before being caught near Dausa.Bainsla had on Monday given a starkly different account. He claimed a group of 22-23 bikers was riding aggressively, repeatedly overtaking his car and slowing down in front of it.He said Shivani suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn, leaving him with little time to react. "I tried very hard to avoid the collision," he had said, denying that he had hit her deliberately or fled when asked to stop at a signal.Police had taken suo motu cognisance of Shivani's video on Monday and registered an FIR against unknown persons under sections 125 and 281, for rash or negligent acts endangering life or personal safety.On Tuesday, the Sector 56 SHO visited Shivani's Delhi home and got her statement recorded. BNS sections 78 and 79 - for physical/digital stalking and insulting a woman's modesty through words or gestures - were added too. The attempt to murder charge was included later.Bainsla, who runs a gym and deals in property as well, identifies himself as a kabaddi and rugby player. The Ciaz he was driving on Sunday belongs to his friend Manish, an Army personnel, who had lent it to him on Friday.
Article Summary: Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into a biker and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday morning, was arrested at Dausa in Rajasthan on Tuesday. A video from her bike's camera that Shivani Chauhan (27) uploaded online showed her being knocked down near Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station after the car repeatedly tried to get alongside her bike. After examining the video of the crash, police have added the attempt to murder charge in the FIR.

Article Title: Wife’s ‘where’re you?’ calls trap highway robbery kingpin
Article Text:
(AI image) Police busted a highway robbery gang after a suspect's wife repeatedly called him





MADURAI: A highway robbery gang was busted after a suspect’s wife repeatedly called him to ask why he was late and when he would return home. Mobile tower records helped Tamil Nadu police trace the gang to Madhya Pradesh. Alleged mastermind Makasud Khan, 35, was arrested and remanded in judicial custody in Tuticorin on Monday. A hunt is on for his remaining four aides.Police said the gang targeted women passengers carrying valuables in handbags left on bus seats during refreshment breaks at highway dhabas. Travelling in an SUV, they stole 173 sovereigns of gold in five incidents in Tuticorin, Oddanchatram, Batlagundu, Aravakurichi and Ulundurpet.The Tuticorin case surfaced on Aug 27, when three men entered a private bus during a halt at Kayathar. One stayed near the front, another guarded the doorway, while a third stole assistant professor Juliet Jeyakumar’s bag. She was carrying about 40 sovereigns of gold jewellery to Chennai for her son’s proposed marriage.She immediately alerted police, and a Kayathar station team secured recordings from the roadside eatery and cameras installed inside the bus.The footage clearly showed the suspects, but investigators initially had no clue to their identities.Officers then examined phone traffic around the location and found one number having received four calls from Madhya Pradesh, while the remaining communications were linked to Tamil Nadu. The number was traced to Makasud’s wife. Police said she repeatedly called after he failed to return as expected, though he had told her he would leave for home on Aug 31.Investigators then shared video grabs of Makasud with Madhya Pradesh police, who identified him as a notorious robber from Kherwan Jagir village in Dhar district. A special team led by Inspector Vanamamalai travelled to Madhya Pradesh. “While heading to the hilltop village, officers unexpectedly spotted Makasud riding a motorcycle in the opposite direction. The team was travelling in a private vehicle, but Makasud tried to flee after spotting police. He was intercepted by officers stationed at a checkpoint near the foothill,” said Vanamamalai.Further questioning linked Makasud’s group to a string of similar offences in Tamil Nadu between Aug 24 and 31. Police said Tuticorin was their final operation before they returned to Madhya Pradesh. Accused was produced before a local court, brought to Tamil Nadu on a transit warrant and remanded on Monday.Investigators said usable video evidence was available only in the Batlagundu and Kayathar cases, restricting recovery to property linked to those incidents. About 388 grams of gold was recovered, while jewellery connected to the remaining three cases is yet to be recovered.
Article Summary: Alleged mastermind Makasud Khan, 35, was arrested and remanded in judicial custody in Tuticorin on Monday. Police said the gang targeted women passengers carrying valuables in handbags left on bus seats during refreshment breaks at highway dhabas. Mobile tower records helped Tamil Nadu police trace the gang to Madhya Pradesh.

Article Title: ‘She is in a lot of pain, has hidden bruises’: Gurgaon biker’s father; Sia to undergo MRI, X-rays today
Article Text:
Her father said Sia was in considerable pain and that some injuries may become apparent only later.

Sia says she was chased, deliberately hit

‘Not hit-and-run, but attempt to murder’: Sia’s advocate

Poll Vote & Share your view Which measure do you think would be most effective in improving road safety? Better traffic monitoring Stronger enforcement of traffic rules Greater public awareness Faster police response 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With agency inputs)





GURGAON: The woman biker injured in the Gurgaon Golf Course Road hit-and-run case will undergo X-rays, MRI scans and other treatment at a Delhi hospital, her father said, as she continued to experience pain from injuries sustained in the collision.Her father said Sia was in considerable pain and that some injuries may become apparent only later.He said she had several hidden bruises following the incident and would visit a hospital in Delhi on Wednesday for X-rays, MRIs and whatever treatment she requires.“After an injury, you often discover later where you have actually been hurt, such as hidden bruises, and she had quite a few of those,” Sia’s father told news agency ANI.Sia also said she was in pain and would undergo further medical tests for some of her injuries. “MLC has been done. For a few injuries, MRI tests and X-ray have to be done,” she told news agency ANI.Sia alleged that the accused and others in the car had harassed her before the collision and deliberately rammed into her vehicle.“Whatever happened to me on Sunday morning was recorded on my video.I have told the Magistrate what I faced personally. I was chased, harassed, and intentionally hit; I could have died,” she added.She said she had given her statement before the magistrate and requested the strictest action in the case.Haryana Police have arrested primary accused Kalyan Bainsla from Dausa, Rajasthan, along with co-occupant Lovneesh from Palwal, after they allegedly fled the scene and switched off their phones.Sia and her family have maintained that the collision on Golf Course Road was an intentional attack and not an accident.Her father also described the incident as an attempt to murder and thanked police for arresting the accused.Sia's advocate, Abhishek, said the case was registered under attempted murder provisions based on the manner in which the vehicle hit her and the accused fled the spot."The charges that have been filed are for attempted murder. As is evident from the video, this is not a hit-and-run case; it is an attempt to murder case. Of course, one cannot comment conclusively on the specific intent of the accused at this stage. That is something the investigation will establish. However, the manner in which the victim was struck and the accused then fled the scene raises serious questions and, on that basis, the case has been registered as attempted murder rather than merely a hit-and-run incident," he told news agency ANI.
Article Summary: Sia will undergo X-rays, MRI scans and other treatment at a Delhi hospital. Her father said Sia was in considerable pain and that some injuries may become apparent only later. Sia and her family have maintained that the collision on Golf Course Road was an intentional attack and not an accident.

Article Title: Raids on Anbil Mahesh pure political Vendetta to mask govt's critical failures: MK Stalin
Article Text:
DMK Chief MK Stalin strongly criticized the state government's recent raids on former minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi.





CHENNAI: DMK Chief MK Stalin launched a scathing attack on the state govt following raids on former school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, calling it a desperate weapon deployed by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s failing administration.Highlighting a series of escalating crises in his social media post, Stalin questioned the governance priorities of CM Vijay.Stalin continued in the same vein and listed out the law and order problems: state-wide power cuts triggering massive public outrage, agitations by Pattinapakkam fishermen, protests outside the Secretariat by families of missing persons in Nepal awaiting answers, a shortage of Aavin milk, the brutal double murder in Ramanathapuram, the horrific beating and murder of a state bus driver during the Pillaiyar Chaturthi procession in Chennai, and the harassment of a woman police officer by a TVK functionary in Ayanavaram."While the state unravels under these critical failures, the CM is completely oblivious, busy shooting in London," MK Stalin charged.Attributing the raids directly to administrative failure and political cowardice, the DMK leader said: "Unable to resolve these pressing public issues, this incompetent TVK govt has unleashed raids as weapons against former minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi. It is purely to divert public attention."Condemning the action, MK Stalin noted that they would fight this blatant act of political vendetta legally. Raiding opposition leaders will not silence public anger. "This govt will soon realise that baseless allegations will never hold up in a court of law," he added.
Article Summary: DMK Chief MK Stalin launched a scathing attack on the state govt following raids on former school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi. He called it a desperate weapon deployed by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s failing administration.

Article Title: Nagpur horror: Woman’s car crashes into pavement, 5 injured; locals demand arrest
Article Text:
A car driven by a woman struck children playing near Gond Mohalla late Tuesday night.





NAGPUR: A car rashly driven by a woman ploughed into the pavement, where children were playing near Gond Mohalla between Gittikhadan Chowk and Dinshaw factory late Tuesday night.Of the five critically injured, one is a two-year-old kid, Vanshika Kulmethe, and her uncle. Eyewitnesses said, the woman was driving under the influence of liquor. The accident triggered massive public outrage even as the injured battled for life at hospital.By midnight, over 500 residents of Gond Mohalla and adjoining areas laid siege to the Gittikhadan police station, demanding immediate arrest of the woman driver.The mob wrecked the woman’s car even as cops kept the woman driver hidden in the police station to shield her from public wrath. Senior officers rushed to the spot and heavy bandobast was deployed.The woman, reportedly from an affluent family, has been rounded up, though she is yet to be named accused, till reports last came in. The process of registering the offence is underway. Locals insisted she must be named in an FIR for rash driving and endangering lives. Police are investigating the case and assured strict action. The condition of the critically injured children remains a matter of concern, with doctors attending to them at the hospital.
Article Summary: Of the five critically injured, one is a two-year-old kid, Vanshika Kulmethe, and her uncle. Eyewitnesses said, the woman was driving under the influence of liquor. The woman, reportedly from an affluent family, has been rounded up, though she is yet to be named accused.

Article Title: Canada deports Lawrence gang's 'logistics manager'
Article Text:
Deo was taken into custody by Punjab Police upon his arrival at Delhi airport





LUDHIANA: The deportation of key operative Karamveer Singh Deo from Canada marks a significant breakthrough for Punjab Police in smashing a vital international logistical network of La-wrence Bishnoi's gang.Deo of Bahadurke, wanted in connection with at least three cases in Ludhiana, was returned to India on Tuesday.Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) records indicate he faces five FIRs alleging murder, attempted murder, extortion, cheating, and forgery.Police allege Deo played a central role in securing forged travel documents for members of Lawrence's gang, including his brother Anmol, who fled India while wanted for the murder of singer Shubhdeep Singh 'Sidhu Moosewala'.The AGTF said Mohali police had registered an FIRunder charges of extortion, forgery, and the Passport Act against Lawrence Bishnoi , Deo, and several associates, leading to six arrests, so far.They report that Deo previously shot Gurwinder Singh 'Bunty Bajwa' over a municipal election dispute on June 10, 2012.After securing bail from the Nabha jail, Deo used a fraudulent passport to flee abroad, later escaping from the US using forged documents in 2020. While overseas, Deo allegedly arranged housing and logistics for Lawrence's gang.His international profile emerged publicly in 2023 when a video from his wedding featured Punjabi singers Karan Aujla and Sherry Mann, performing alongside Anmol Bishnoi and Deo.Deo's criminal record in Ludhiana dates to 2012, beginning with the murder of a former sarpanch's husband, Gurwinder Singh.He was subsequently charged in 2014 with cheating and forgery at the Haibowal police station.On June 20, 2026, police nominated Deo in a case of attempted murder following a shooting during a property dispute in Salem Tabri.Foreign police had investigated Deo after shots were fired at the house of singer A P Dhillon, though a local court later cleared him of involvement in that incident.A senior police officer said: "Karamveer is a key operative of Lawrence Bishnoi's gang and has a long association with its boss. Since fleeing abroad, Karamveer has sheltered Lawrence's henchmen and provided them with logistics to execute crime."The officer added: "Karamveer would be questioned on how and who all he helped by arranging fake passports to escape abroad after crime,"
Article Summary: Deo of Bahadurke, wanted in connection with at least three cases in Ludhiana, was returned to India on Tuesday. He faces five FIRs alleging murder, attempted murder, extortion, cheating, and forgery. Deo allegedly arranged housing and logistics for Lawrence Bishnoi's gang.

Article Title: ‘Will show reality’: CJP’s Saurabh Das brings ‘School Theek Karo’ to Noida, urges youth to inspect schools
Article Text:
Party spokesperson Saurabh Das announced plans for a comprehensive school audit

CJP’s ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign





NOIDA: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) on Tuesday took its ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign to Noida, with party spokesperson Saurabh Das announcing an audit of schools in the city and urging young people across Uttar Pradesh to inspect institutions in their own neighbourhoods.Das said the team would visit schools in Noida to assess the conditions in which children are studying and document the findings.He said Noida was considered one of the better districts in Uttar Pradesh and that the team would assess whether its schools matched that perception."Today, we’ve come to Noida. We’re going to audit some schools here as part of our 'School Theek Karo' campaign. We’ll see the conditions in which children are studying. Noida is one of the better districts in UP, so hopefully, the school conditions will be good too. Whatever the situation is, we’ll show you the reality."The CJP spokesperson also appealed to young people in Uttar Pradesh to take up school audits in their respective areas and document the conditions of schools and the education being provided to children."We want young people from UP to go out and audit schools as well—to show what condition the schools in their neighbourhoods are in and what kind of education children are receiving.Today, we’re planning to visit schools in Noida, but we’d encourage other young people to take on this responsibility too and audit schools in their own areas..." Das said.The CJP had launched its nationwide ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign in August, describing it as a social-audit drive focused on government schools and basic facilities.The campaign calls on citizens and volunteers to inspect schools and document issues related to infrastructure and essential amenities.The campaign’s first audit was conducted at a government school in Santuk Pimpri village of Maharashtra’s Hingoli district, where CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke highlighted issues including lack of drinking water, benches, dirty washrooms, broken windows and inadequate water supply.Subsequent CJP audits have also focused on classrooms, drinking-water facilities, toilets, benches and material used for preparing midday meals.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: CJP’s ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign launched in August. Party spokesperson Saurabh Das announced plans for a comprehensive school audit in Noida. Das also urged young people across Uttar Pradesh to inspect institutions in their own neighbourhoods.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan founded a school, 10 years later and after $125 million in donation, Board voted to close it after learning that …
Article Text:
Why the Board voted to close the school founded by Priscilla Chan

Mixed results and challenges

Impact on families and community

Lessons in philanthropy

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg ’s wife Priscilla Chan co-founded the Primary School in East Palo Alto, California in 2016 with the backing of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI). The school was designed to serve low-income families, the tuition fee private school aimed to support the “whole child” through wraparound services such as dental checkups, wellness coaching, and early‑intervention screenings. Over ten years, CZI poured more than $125 million into the project, making it one of the most ambitious philanthropic education ventures in Silicon Valley. However, despite the strong support services and community engagement, academic performance often fell short of state norms, complicating efforts to replicate the model in public and charter schools. A report by Wall Street Journal revealed that despite all these efforts the school shut its doors this past June after a decade of operation.In April 2025, the school’s board voted unanimously to shut down after learning CZI would not continue funding beyond the 2025‑26 academic year. Board president Jean‑Claude Brizard said the decision was made in alignment with its largest funder. A CZI spokesperson emphasized that the closure was the board’s choice and that the organization’s focus had shifted toward scientific research.The closure reflects a broader shift at CZI, which has moved its philanthropic focus away from social issues and toward scientific research in recent years.Around the same time the organization narrowed its mission, telling staff that funding for social advocacy work had been scaled back to better match its focus as a science-oriented philanthropy, the board's vote to close the school followed. Brizard described the timing relative to Zuckerberg and Chan's attendance at President Trump's inauguration as an unfortunate coincidence, and CZI said there was no evidence the inauguration influenced the board's decision.By some measures, the school struggled to meet expectations. Academic performance often fell short of state norms, complicating efforts to replicate its model in public and charter schools. High principal turnover and structural challenges also hindered progress. Yet, the school succeeded in areas beyond academics: students showed improvements in well‑being, socio‑emotional skills, and health outcomes. About 85% of students had annual well‑child visits, compared with 55% of children on Medicaid in the county.Nearly 540 children were enrolled across two campuses when the closure was announced. Parents described the decision as “crushing,” with one calling the school a “godsend.” The Ravenswood City Elementary School District is now preparing for an enrollment surge. To ease the transition, CZI pledged $50 million, covering the school’s lease and supporting local groups, along with education savings accounts for families.The Primary School’s closure highlights the difficulty of sustaining philanthropic education projects. As Rick Hess of the American Enterprise Institute noted, “Business leaders look at K‑12 education and go, ‘Man, how hard can it be to improve this thing?’ Well, it’s incredibly hard.” Chan herself admitted outcomes weren’t where “anyone would have wanted them to be.”
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan co-founded the Primary School in East Palo Alto, California in 2016 with the backing of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) The school was designed to serve low-income families, the tuition fee private school aimed to support the “whole child” Over ten years, CZI poured more than $125 million into the project, making it one of the most ambitious philanthropic education ventures in Silicon Valley.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: Digital arrest: 88-year-old loses Rs 78L In 10-day ordeal in Delhi
Article Text:
An 88-year-old woman was digitally held for ten days by scammers (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: An 88-year-old woman from southeast Delhi's Sarita Vihar was allegedly kept under digital arrest for around 10 days by scammers who told her that she was linked to a money laundering case and coerced her into transferring Rs 78 lakh from her bank accounts.The woman, who lives alone as her children reside elsewhere, got a call around 5.30 pm on Aug 24. The caller allegedly told her that a money laundering case had been registered in connection with her bank accounts. The fraudsters reportedly showed her images purportedly depicting conversations involving several people, including a senior judicial official, and told her that they would help her get out of the alleged legal trouble and protect her family from any action.According to her complaint, the fraudsters then placed her under continuous surveillance and instructed her to report back to them every hour. She was also allegedly directed to keep her phone camera switched on throughout the night. The callers allegedly used multiple mobile numbers and WhatsApp calls to communicate with her.The fraudsters also allegedly made her download and use a social media application for communication.The woman transferred Rs 51 lakh from one of her bank accounts on Sept 1. On Sept 2, she transferred another Rs 27 lakh from another account through RTGS.The suspects allegedly instructed her to delete WhatsApp messages containing details of the bank accounts and transactions. They also warned her against informing anyone else about the matter. The woman continued following their instructions until Sept 2, when the fraud was eventually discovered by her family.The incident came to light after her elder daughter received an email notification from a bank regarding the Rs 27 lakh RTGS transaction made on Sept 2. The woman's son-in-law, who lives in Gurgaon, subsequently visited her residence that evening. It was then that the family became aware of the alleged fraud.The woman subsequently reported the matter on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP), where a complaint was registered on Sept 2. Her daughter also filed a complaint on her behalf on Sept 3.The fraudsters continued calling her until Sept 4, but she stopped answering the calls.Police said an inquiry was conducted by Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit of Delhi Police . Based on the inquiry, an FIR was registered under Sections 318(4), 319, 340 and 61(2) of BNS. The sections relate to cheating, impersonation, offences involving forged documents or electronic records, and criminal conspiracy.
Article Summary: The woman, who lives alone as her children reside elsewhere, got a call around 5.30 pm on Aug 24. The caller allegedly told her that a money laundering case had been registered in connection with her bank accounts. The fraudsters reportedly showed her images purportedly depicting conversations involving several people, including a senior judicial official. The incident came to light after her elder daughter received an email notification from a bank.

Article Title: Disha Salian death: What CBI will investigate after FIR—from police records to key witnesses
Article Text:
The CBI is investigating Disha Salian's 2020 death, examining police records and the prior inquiry. Investigators will scrutinize evidence, witness statements, and forensic materials from the case

Police records, earlier inquiry first

Forensic, autopsy records and witnesses

Names mentioned in FIR

What did Bombay HC say?

Seema Pahuja to supervise probe





MUMBAI: The CBI investigation into Disha Salian’s 2020 death will focus on police records and the earlier inquiry, statements from personnel who handled the case, key witnesses, forensic and autopsy material, and the scene of the incident following the registration of an FIR.Disha Salian, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput’s manager, died after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Sushant was found dead at his Bandra residence a week later.Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had approached the high court seeking a murder probe, citing “suspicious circumstances”. He recorded his statement before the CBI last week, which was converted into an FIR on September 13.A CBI official said the FIR was registered pursuant to the court’s direction and that no accused has been named at this stage. Names would be included if involvement is established during the investigation, the official said.The agency is expected to examine documents and allegations linked to the case, including police records and files from the initial inquiry, as well as the actions of personnel who handled the case.The FIR alleges that some public servants and police officers need to be investigated for the destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records; fabrication of official records; and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders.The CBI is also expected to examine autopsy and forensic records and question officials associated with those processes. Security guards at the building are among those likely to be questioned.The team is expected to record statements of people who attended a gathering at the Mumbai home of Disha’s fiancé, Rohan Roy, on the night before her death.The FIR claims: “The persons whose roles require investigation in connection with the commission of the principal offences, criminal conspiracy, subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story, and suppression, destruction and/or fabrication of evidence include Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, Dino Morea, Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya Thackeray’s bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, Sachin Vaze, Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur, Uddhav Thackeray, Anil Deshmukh, API Ashok Devadhe, PI Jagdev Kalapad, PI Shailendra Nagarkar, PI Chimaji Adhav, PI Arjun Rajane, concerned officers of Malvani Police Station. ”The names in the FIR are allegations requiring investigation and do not amount to a finding of guilt.The high court had pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation and observed that the police probe “raised more questions than answers.”The court had also noted that Disha’s family had not been provided with the post-mortem report or the accidental death report.On September 2, while ordering a CBI probe, the high court directed the agency that no one should be named as an accused unless there was evidence against them.CBI officer Seema Pahuja will supervise the investigation, sources said. She will be assisted by investigating officer Deputy SP Puran Kumar and others.Pahuja is currently posted as an SP with the special crimes unit at the CBI headquarters in Delhi.
Article Summary: Disha Salian, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput’s manager, died after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Investigators will scrutinize evidence, witness statements, and forensic materials from the case.

Article Title: ‘She shared information about Aaditya Thackeray’s illegal activities with Sushant’: What Disha Salian’s father’s lawyer alleged
Article Text:
The CBI is now investigating Disha Salian's death following her father's allegations

What Disha’s father’s lawyer alleged

What the CBI FIR says

HC flagged discrepancies in probe





MUMBAI: Satish Salian, father of actor Sushant Singh Rajput’s former manager Disha Salian, has alleged lapses in the investigation into her death, with the CBI now examining the case following an FIR registered on September 13.Disha, who worked as Sushant’s manager, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai. Sushant was found dead at his Bandra residence nearly a week later.Satish Salian had approached the Bombay high court seeking a murder probe, citing what he described as suspicious circumstances surrounding his daughter’s death. He recorded his statement before the CBI last week, and the statement was subsequently converted into an FIR.Satish Salian’s advocate Nilesh Ojha alleged that Disha had information about alleged illegal activities involving Aaditya Thackeray. According to Ojha’s allegation, Disha shared the information with Sushant, who discussed it with Rhea Chakraborty. Ojha further alleged that the information was subsequently passed on to Aaditya Thackeray, following which the alleged offence and an alleged cover-up took place.These are allegations made on behalf of Disha’s father and have not been established by the investigation.The CBI has registered the FIR pursuant to the high court’s direction. An official said no accused has been named at this stage and that names would be added if their involvement is established during the probe.The FIR says the roles of certain public servants and police officers need to be examined in connection with allegations of destruction or suppression of case papers and other public records, fabrication of official records, and alleged misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery to shield offenders.It also calls for the questioning of forensic and autopsy officials, police personnel involved in the initial inquiry and others, including security guards at the building where Disha died.The FIR lists several individuals whose roles, it says, require investigation in connection with the alleged principal offences, conspiracy, the subsequent creation and propagation of what it describes as a false suicide narrative, and alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.The names mentioned in the FIR include Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, Dino Morea, Sooraj Pancholi, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, Sachin Vaze, Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur, Uddhav Thackeray, Anil Deshmukh and several police officers. The FIR does not by itself establish guilt against any of those named.The Bombay high court, while dealing with Salian’s petition, had questioned why Mumbai Police had not registered an FIR in the case despite nearly six years having passed. The court pointed to what it called “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation and observed that the police probe had “raised more questions than answers.”The court had also taken note of the fact that Disha’s family had not been provided her post-mortem report or accidental death report.On September 2, the high court ordered a CBI probe and directed the agency not to name anyone as an accused unless there was evidence establishing their involvement.The CBI investigation is now expected to examine the documents and allegations, record statements of police personnel involved in the initial inquiry, inspect the scene and question key witnesses. Investigators are also expected to conduct forensic and technical analysis before deciding whom to question further.
Article Summary: The CBI is now investigating Disha Salian's death following her father's allegations. Disha, who worked as Sushant’s manager, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai. Satish Salian had approached the Bombay high court seeking a murder probe.

Article Title: TC suspended, inquiry initiated over girl’s ordeal; no action yet against RPF constable
Article Text:
Representational pic





Mumbai: Central Railway has suspended ticket checker Rajendra Tribhuvan and initiated an inquiry into the incident involving a 17-year-old schoolgirl who was allegedly taken between several stations following a dispute over an AC travel fare.“Tribhuvan has been suspended and an inquiry has been initiated into the matter,” CR officials said.The decision about suspension was conveyed to the girl’s parents too after her mother met a senior CR official at CR headquarters on Tuesday. However, the parents are upset that no action had been taken against the RPF personnel who “made her feel like a criminal”.CR officials said Tribhuvan had initially joined the railways as a Class IV employee and subsequently became a ticket checker after successfully clearing the department’s internal examination.The Class 12 student, who was travelling alone in an AC local on Sept 11, had a valid First Class ticket but was unaware that a separate travel authority was required for AC travel. Her parents had alleged that after the fare dispute, she was taken from Mansarovar to Panvel and subsequently to Wadala Road, despite her mother travelling to collect her.At Panvel, Dhumal became involved in the matter. The parents alleged that the constable refused to identify herself initially and spoke harshly to the girl’s father on the phone.They were later told that the girl would be taken to Belapur, but she was eventually taken to Wadala Road.The girl’s father had alleged that his daughter was handled “like a criminal” and said she had undergone counselling to help her overcome the trauma.CR had earlier said its inquiry found no evidence that the minor was deliberately abandoned. It said that after she was identified as a minor, instructions were issued for her safe handover at Wadala Road and that she was handed over to a railway employee who represented that he was known to the family, in the presence of RPF and other railway staff.The railway had also said the concerned personnel were counselled to exercise greater care while dealing with minors and ensure properly verified handovers.
Article Summary: Central Railway has suspended ticket checker Rajendra Tribhuvan and initiated an inquiry into the incident. The 17-year-old schoolgirl was allegedly taken between several stations following a dispute over an AC travel fare. The Class 12 student had a valid First Class ticket but was unaware that a separate travel authority was required for AC travel.
